# List with search and filters — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for list with search and filters when the block should own the finding while the host owns the rows: query and filter state over row data. The block owns the query and the filter model while the host owns rows and the facet adapters, with `filterable` defaulting to reading each row's own fields so flat row models need no adapter and `searchable` adding extra match terms per row. Variant and density pass straight to the underlying list presets, the filter bar stays uncontrolled inside by default with the query trio taking over when the host needs it, and the full filter modal stays host-owned behind the open-filters request exactly as with the standalone bar. The idle empty state and the query-aware empty state are different blocks — no query with no filters is not the same state as a query with no hits — because there is no server search: rows are in memory and remote data pages through the host before it reaches the block. The search, the bar and the rows announce as one labelled section.

## Native

### Features

Reach for list with search and filters when the block should own the finding while the host owns the rows: query and filter state over row data — the native twin under the same contract. The block owns the query and the filter model while the host owns rows and the facet adapters, with `filterable` defaulting to reading each row's own fields so flat row models need no adapter and `searchable` adding extra match terms per row. Variant and density pass straight to the underlying list presets, the filter bar stays uncontrolled inside by default with the query trio taking over when the host needs it, and the full filter sheet stays host-owned behind the open-filters request exactly as with the standalone bar. The idle empty state and the query-aware empty state are different blocks — no query with no filters is not the same state as a query with no hits — because there is no server search: rows are in memory and remote data pages through the host before it reaches the block. The search, the facets and the rows announce as one labelled unit under the host's accessible label.
